title: The Day the Leftover Candy Unionized
skyStory: A skinny eleven percent moon is lounging in Sagittarius, still wearing last night's costume and refusing to admit Halloween is over. Mars keeps hinting that the plastic skeleton on the porch should come down. Saturn has quietly filed the jack-o'-lanterns under compost. Outside, the maples are dropping their last leaves in dramatic little swoons, like actors who were told the play closes Friday.

reading: November arrives with a gust that slams one door in the house for no reason. Treat it as a starting pistol. You have nine days left in this year of readings, and the cabin wants its woodpile stacked neatly before the final chapter.

Around 10:20 am you will be tempted to start a project the size of a barn. The [[Knight of Wands]] snorts into its gauntlet. One shelf, one drawer, one email folder. Finish it so thoroughly it sparkles. Then sit back and admire it for a full minute, which is longer than you think, and do not use the minute to plan the next one.
joel.mission: Pick the single smallest unfinished thing in your home and finish it before noon, then announce its completion to an empty room.
joel.omen: A pumpkin sitting on a step with a slightly smug face. It means a small job is waiting to be called done.
joel.elementWhy: the first November gust clears the deck

reading: The tide went out further than usual this morning, and the Wood Rat noticed before anyone else. Something small and shiny got left behind on the sand of your day. Maybe a forgotten idea, maybe a note from last week. Pick it up.

By mid-afternoon someone will ask you to explain a thing you know inside out. Your hands will start moving before your mouth does, and that is how everyone will know the story is going to be good. Life Path 11 hums along underneath like a radiator. Let one listener walk away a level higher than they arrived. That is your quiet November magic.
nancy.mission: Rescue one fun-sized leftover from Halloween and give it to someone as if it were a medal of honour.
nancy.omen: A wet leaf stuck flat to a window, shaped almost like a hand. Someone nearby is about to wave hello in a big way.

together.text: Each of you describe last night's best costume you saw, real or imagined, in exactly seven words. Swap them. The more ridiculous description wins custody of the skeleton for one imaginary week.

title: The Day of the Rogue Umbrella
skyStory: The crescent has fattened to seventeen percent and is still hanging around Sagittarius, packing a backpack with snacks it will never eat. Rain rolls in sideways off the water. Mars is excited, because sideways rain is basically weather with a sword. Saturn has put on galoshes and is pretending it chose this. Somewhere a wind chime is playing jazz.

reading: The Tiger wakes up with a spark already lit, and by 9 am you will have two brilliant ideas and a third that is mostly a pun. Keep the pun. It is the only one with legs.

An umbrella will betray you today, either flipping inside out or hiding in the wrong car. This is not bad luck. It is the [[Six of Pentacles]] engineering a chance for someone to share theirs, and you must say yes without immediately offering to carry their bag in return. Huddle. Accept the shelter. Fire that is protected from the rain burns longer, and frankly the Tiger looks great slightly damp.
joel.mission: Tell one person a genuinely good idea of yours and then stop talking for five full seconds to see what they add.
joel.omen: A red umbrella blowing past with nobody holding it. Your idea is ready to travel without you steering.
joel.elementWhy: a spark that refuses to get soggy

reading: Your intuition is running a few minutes ahead of the clock today. At some point you will think of a person and, within the hour, hear from them. Do not act surprised. Act like you scheduled it.

Rainy Sagittarius moons make everyone want adventure but nobody want to leave the house. You are the exception: you can have an adventure from the couch, because you are the one who tells it. Pick a tiny memory, a ferry ride or a strange café or a dog with a hat, and polish it into a story with a twist ending. The ruby on your pinky will catch the lamplight every time you gesture. Gesture a lot.
nancy.mission: Write a one-line weather report for your own mood and post it on the fridge like an official bulletin.
nancy.omen: Two raindrops racing down a window. Bet on the left one. If it wins, an easy yes is coming.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's fire keeps the rain off

together.text: Trade one idea each that you have been too shy to say out loud. No critique allowed, only the phrase 'and what if' to build on it. Three rounds maximum, or the idea gets too big for the cabin door.

title: The Moon Climbs Nancy's Mountain
skyStory: The moon has crossed into Capricorn, Nancy's own sign, a quarter lit and puffing slightly from the climb. It has brought a thermos and a very serious hiking map. Saturn, who rules this mountain, rolls out a welcome mat it knitted itself. Mars watches from a lower ledge, impressed and pretending not to be. Frost glitters on the windshields at dawn like the sky dusted for company.

reading: With the moon visiting Nancy's sign, your job today is to be the good neighbour at the foot of the mountain. Keep the chimney going. Wave when you see a light up top.

Around 1:45 pm you will catch yourself rushing something that does not need to be rushed. Capricorn energy moves like a mountain goat: slow, sure, and somehow always at the summit first. Try it. Walk at half speed from your desk to the kettle and notice three things you usually miss. One of them will be funny. Tell Nancy about it, because today she is technically the landlord of the sky.
joel.mission: Move the onyx to your giving wrist before your first coffee and leave it there until the streetlights blink on, sending steady strength up the mountain.
joel.omen: Frost shaped like a little peak on a car roof. Nancy's mountain is saying thanks for the strength.
joel.stoneWhy: matching her pinky for the day

reading: The moon is in your house today and it has put its feet up on your coffee table. You are allowed to be the host who also relaxes. Saturn, your ruler, says even mountains take a seat sometimes.

Expect to be quietly correct about something at least twice before supper. The Wood Rat spots the flaw in a plan, the typo in a sign, the reason the printer is sulking. You may choose to fix one and simply smile at the other. Tonight, before bed, stand by a window for one breath and look up. The quarter moon is in your sign and it would love a wave from the owner.
nancy.mission: Give one person a compliment so specific it makes them squint, like praising the exact angle of their scarf.
nancy.omen: Hoofprints in the frost, or a lone figure climbing a steep hill. Your patience is about to reach a summit.

together.text: Since the moon is staying on Nancy's mountain, Joel sends one photo of something steady and Nancy replies with one photo of something sparkly. Together they make a postcard from the summit. Keep it as the moon's guestbook entry.

title: The Day of the Half-Lit Staircase
skyStory: First quarter moon, exactly half lit and half shadow, still parked in Capricorn like a careful driver checking its mirrors. It looks like a light switch somebody left in the middle position. Saturn approves of the balance. Mars wants to flip it all the way on. The wind off the water argues both sides and then leaves early.

reading: Half moon, halfway decisions. You will be standing on the middle step of something today, an email half written or a plan half drawn, and your instinct will be to leap to the top. The [[Knight of Wands]] suggests taking one stair at a time, loudly, like a tiger climbing a creaky porch.

Around 4:10 pm the light will hit something in your room at an angle you have never noticed. Stop and look. Half light is when the cabin shows its secrets: dust motes, a scratch in the floor with a story, a forgotten note under a lamp. Finish one half-thing before dark and the moon will consider you even.
joel.mission: Find one task you started last week and finish only the next single step, then stop on purpose and grin.
joel.omen: A staircase with exactly one light bulb out. Proceed anyway; you know the way better than you think.
joel.elementWhy: one firm step at a time

reading: The [[Six of Swords]] drifts by on a grey November tide, the little boat halfway across the water. That is exactly where today feels. The far shore is visible and the near one is getting smaller. Nothing to rush. Joel has an oar.

Today the Mountain is unusually good at noticing what is already done. Make a quiet list in your head while you wash a cup or walk to the car: three things you have finished this year that nobody gave you a medal for. Then give yourself the medal. The stacked diamonds on your left middle finger will flash when you get to number three, which is how the sky applauds.
nancy.mission: Say out loud, to anyone or to the kettle, one thing you finished this year that deserves a parade.
nancy.omen: A boat or a picture of one, pointed toward the right. The crossing is going better than it feels.

together.text: Each of you pick one thing to finish by Nov 9, when this year of readings closes. Tell each other what it is in six words or fewer. On the last day, report back like sailors home from sea.

title: The Day the Kettle Had an Idea
skyStory: Forty-three percent lit and newly arrived in Aquarius, the moon has traded its hiking boots for a lab coat. It is inventing things. Most of them are useless, like a spoon with a tiny umbrella, and it is delighted anyway. Saturn checks the safety goggles. Mars wants to press the big red button. Outside, the first proper gale of November tests every gutter in town.

reading: Aquarius moon, inventor energy, and the Tiger already has the tool box out. Today the best idea you have will arrive while you wait for water to boil. Do not walk away from the kettle. Stand there like a man guarding treasure.

Courage today is not loud. It is sending the message you rewrote four times, as written on the fourth try, and then closing the laptop. It is saying 'I could use a hand with this' before 2 pm, with no apology attached. The [[Six of Pentacles]] is leaning on the counter, watching to see whether you ask. Ask, and something kind will come back faster than the kettle clicks.
joel.mission: Ask someone for a small favour today without explaining why or offering anything in return. Just say thank you.
joel.omen: A kettle clicking off at the exact moment you sit down. Receiving looks good on you.
joel.stoneWhy: soft shine for a brave ask
joel.elementWhy: the kettle is the oracle today

reading: The gale outside is loud, but you are louder in the best way. Today you get to be the one who says the bold thing in the meeting, the chat, or the kitchen. The Wood Rat has done the research. The Mountain has the patience. Now the Fire gets a turn.

Someone will try to explain a plan with too many steps. You will see the shortcut in about four seconds. Share it kindly, with your hands drawing the shape of it in the air, and watch the room go quiet. That quiet is respect. Write the shortcut down afterward; Aquarius likes a patent, even an imaginary one.
nancy.mission: Invent a completely useless gadget out loud, give it a name, and describe it to someone with total sincerity.
nancy.omen: A gutter overflowing in a perfect arc like a fountain. Your bold idea will land beautifully.
nancy.elementWhy: your turn to carry the torch

together.text: Before supper, one small brave thing apiece: a hard call, a bold sentence, a new route home. At bedtime, trade a single emoji describing how it went. Fire meets Mountain, and both report victory.

title: The Day of the Windblown Lists
skyStory: A slightly-over-half moon, fifty-three percent lit, is lounging in Aquarius and running an experiment on coincidence. It has written the same strange note twice and handed both copies to the gale. Saturn says this is unscientific. Mars says it is hilarious. The wind from the shore delivers the test materials personally, one gust at a time.

reading: Somewhere along your route today, a gust will slap a folded scrap of paper against your leg. It is somebody's to-do list in loopy blue pen: fix the weathervane, call the lighthouse, find the very small ladder. Take a photo. Then tuck it somewhere dry, in case its owner comes looking.

Here is the twist: Nancy will catch one too, within the same hour, different handwriting, same three chores. Neither of you will believe it at first. Don't even scream when the photos arrive side by side. The moon in Aquarius loves a pattern, and the [[Wheel of Fortune]] gets one spin today just to make you both laugh. ΔΕΣ, Tiger. Then wonder, seriously, how small that ladder is.
joel.mission: Photograph the most cheerful lost object you see today and caption it as if it were a famous explorer.
joel.omen: A scrap of paper tumbling uphill against the wind. The universe is reviewing your week favourably.

reading: The Wood Rat sees it first, of course: a scrap of paper pinned to a fence post by the gale, flapping like it wants your attention. You will unfold it and feel a funny prickle on the back of your neck, the Life Path 11 kind, the kind that means a story is about to happen.

Send the photo before you think too hard. When Joel's photo comes back with the very same list, tiny ladder and all, you will laugh so hard your hands do a whole interpretive dance. DES, Mountain. This is the sky reminding you that the two of you are tuned to the same channel, even across a gale. Save both pictures. They deserve a frame, or at least a folder.
nancy.mission: Leave a little note for a lost object you find today: 'Your human is looking for you. Stay put.'
nancy.omen: Handwriting that is not yours tucked somewhere it should not be. The other half of a pair is nearby, and it is a happy match.

together.text: Send each other the strangest matching thing you each see today, windblown lists included. Then invent the missing fourth chore together. If you both pick the same one, the moon wins its experiment and you owe it a respectful nod at moonrise. Keep the photos in a folder called Evidence.

title: The Day the Rowboat Got a Name
skyStory: The moon has grown to sixty-three percent in Aquarius and is busy redesigning boats. It insists the oars should be shaped like question marks. Saturn has drawn up proper blueprints anyway. Mars wants a figurehead shaped like a tiger. Out on the grey bay, a cold fog sits on the water like it is waiting for a ferry that left an hour ago.

reading: The [[Six of Swords]] floats into your morning on a calm patch of water. You know this card. It has been in Nancy's corner all year, the crossing not yet finished, the little boat, and you with an oar. Today the boat needs a name.

Think about it while you do ordinary things: folding laundry, waiting at a light, stirring something on the stove. A good boat name is funny and a little brave. It should make you both laugh and feel like heading out anyway. Text it to Nancy by 7 pm. Rowing is easier when the boat has a name painted on its side, and the Tiger is surprisingly good with a paintbrush.
joel.mission: Come up with a name for the rowboat from the Six of Swords and send it to Nancy with a tiny drawing.
joel.omen: A gull standing on a buoy, perfectly still. The crossing is steadier than it looks from inside.
joel.stoneWhy: Nancy's stone, for rowing her way
joel.elementWhy: warmth in the bow of the boat

reading: Fog on the shore this morning, thick enough to hide the far side entirely. That is fine. You do not need to see the other shore to know it is there. You have been rowing toward it with real skill, one patient stroke after another.

Somebody will tell you about their own crossing today, a change or a fresh start, and you will know exactly the right thing to say because you have been on the water too. Say it with your whole heart and both hands. Then let Joel's boat name arrive tonight and make you laugh. [[The Star]] glimmers somewhere behind the fog, and it smells like hope.
nancy.mission: Paint, draw or write the rowboat's name somewhere small, on a sticky note, a mug or the edge of a page.
nancy.omen: A foghorn or a long low sound at dusk. The far shore is close enough to hear.

together.text: Agree on one name for the boat you have been rowing all year. Joel proposes, Nancy approves or improves. Once it is named, the crossing counts as officially charted, and the sky promises calm water for the last two days.

title: The Day the Fog Kept Secrets
skyStory: The moon has slipped into Pisces, seventy-one percent lit and dreamy as a cat in a sunbeam. It is not interested in plans today. It wants to float. Saturn has, astonishingly, agreed to take the afternoon off and is reading a novel. Mars is sulking but also kind of enjoying the quiet. The fog off the water has not lifted since breakfast and does not intend to.

reading: Pisces moon, soft edges everywhere. The Tiger is allowed to nap. Not a strategic nap. A genuine sprawl on the couch with a blanket, a window full of fog, and absolutely nothing being optimized.

Around 3:30 pm a memory from early in this year of readings will drift back to you, maybe a mission you did or a card that kept turning up. Let it play like a home movie. [[The Sun]] has been asking you to allow joy all year instead of earning it, and today is a final chance to practise. Do one thing simply because it is pleasant, then do not tell anyone about it. Some joys are just for you and the cabin.
joel.mission: Spend ten minutes doing nothing useful at all, on purpose, and notice the exact moment the guilt fades.
joel.omen: A candle flame standing perfectly still. Rest is the right answer today.
joel.stoneWhy: soft shine for a soft day

reading: The Wood Rat usually notices everything. Today, let something go unnoticed on purpose. A messy drawer, a strange email, a neighbour's questionable lawn ornament. The fog is covering for you. It is very good at secrets.

Find one quiet half hour this evening, a cup of something warm and a soft lamp. Think back over the year of readings and pick a single day you remember best. Do not explain to yourself why it stuck. Just let it sit there glowing. Tomorrow the year closes, and that memory is your ticket to the final page. The mother of pearl on your ring finger will feel slightly warmer when you have chosen.
nancy.mission: Leave one small mess completely alone today and wish it a pleasant evening when you walk past it.
nancy.omen: A streetlight glowing through fog like a little moon. Your favourite memory from this year is the right one.
nancy.elementWhy: the fog drifts, so do you

together.text: No missions together today. Just send each other one word at bedtime describing how the fog felt. Tomorrow is the final page of this year, and the sky wants you both rested and a little sentimental.

title: The Last Page, Then the Shuffle
skyStory: One year ago the moon was brand new, two percent lit in Sagittarius, pretending to be asleep while this page woke up. Tonight it is eighty percent bright in Pisces and wide awake, misty-eyed. Mars brought the same streamers. Saturn brought the same clipboard, every box ticked. The deck sits on the table, ready to be gathered, shuffled, and dealt again.

reading: A year ago tomorrow, the very first reading told you to plant one seed and walk away whistling. Look at the garden now. The Tiger learned, slowly and with a great deal of grumbling, to say thank you and mean it. That is no small summit.

Tonight, before bed, switch the onyx to your right wrist one last time this year and send all of it up the mountain: the jokes, the missions, the mittens, the rowboat. Then switch it back and let something return. The [[Six of Pentacles]] says the giving and receiving are even now. The cards will be reshuffled tomorrow, and the Fire will be ready.
joel.mission: Find the tiny folded sentence from last November, or write a new one, and read it aloud to the cabin.
joel.omen: A chimney puffing smoke in a straight line, just like the first day. The circle is closed and the fire still burns.

reading: A year ago you turned the ruby outward like a tiny lighthouse, and the sky has been following that beam ever since. Story after story, crossing after crossing, your hands dancing the whole way. The Mountain did not move. It did not need to. Everything came to it.

Tonight the moon is nearly full in Pisces, soft and generous. Set the ruby beside the onyx under a window and let them glow side by side for one breath. Then say thank you to the year in your own words. [[The World]] waits to close the circle. Tomorrow the deck shuffles, a new moon of readings begins, and the Light Returning will be dealt a fresh, bright hand.
nancy.mission: Tell the story of your favourite day this year, with your hands, to someone who has not heard it.
nancy.omen: A gull standing on one leg somewhere it should not be, just like the first day. Bold choices remain in season.
nancy.stoneWhy: the Fire's stone, a year strong

together.text: On the first day you each sent one word for how the month should feel. Tonight, send one word for how the whole year felt. Compare at bedtime. Then the cards get gathered, shuffled and dealt again, and the next adventure begins tomorrow.
